subject: Concourse SDK compatibility: shim request and SLA impact assessment
messages:
From: Erik Stone <erik.stone@concourse.io>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bethany Cho <bethany.cho@concourse.io>, integrations@concourse.io
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Integration: SDK v4 change — compatibility shim & SLA questions

Hi Stephanie,

Heads up: Concourse is intending to ship SDK v4 on 2027-06-15. The release removes the legacy streaming endpoint and replaces the auth header scheme (X-Conc-Auth -> Authorization: Bearer). Several of our mutual customers (including an ISV that bundles Concourse + Redwood) have asked us to coordinate a compatibility plan.

We have two asks for Redwood:
- Can Redwood provide a temporary gateway shim that accepts the v3-style requests and translates them to v4 (auth header mapping + streaming fallback) so partners can upgrade on their own timetable?
- If a shim is possible, what is the expected SLA/latency impact and any cost implications (token accounting, billing changes) we should pass on to partners?

We attached the SDK v4 proposal (concourse_sdk_v4_proposal.pdf) and a short Jira (INT-842). Would appreciate a quick read and an initial call.

Thanks — Erik
Erik Stone
Director, Integrations | Concourse Inc.

Thanks for the heads up, Erik — and for the pdf. We can definitely help explore options. Quick summary of next steps from our side:

1) Internal tech assessment to decide between a) gateway-side translation (edge shim) or b) partner adapter library maintained by Concourse/ISV.
2) Prototype timeline: ~3 weeks for a thin gateway shim that maps headers + routes the old streaming frames to the new stream API (we'll validate replay/ordering).
3) Canary plan: small % of traffic in your staging + one customer pilot; measure latency delta and error delta.

To move fast, can you share: traffic profiles (p50/p95 token sizes), sample v3 requests/headers, and any required certs for auth translation? Also attached a short list of partner questions we typically use.

We can set up a 30-minute tech sync tomorrow if that works for you.

-- Stephanie

Senior Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference

From: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>

Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration: SDK v4 change — compatibility shim & SLA questions

Hi all — read the v4 proposal and sketched out technical options. TL;DR: gateway shim is feasible and lowest friction for partners, but there are tradeoffs we should call out to Concourse and joint customers.

Option A — Gateway shim (Redwood):
- What it does: accept legacy v3 traffic, map X-Conc-Auth -> Authorization, translate streaming frames into the new bidi stream expected by v4, surface identical HTTP endpoints to partners.
- Pros: zero code change for partners, fast to prototype.
- Cons: extra CPU/parse/serialize per request, small memory overhead for buffering streaming frames. Potentially complicates tracing (we'll need to inject span mappings).
- Performance: rough estimate based on similar shims: +8–12ms median latency, +15–35ms p95 depending on payload size. We should run perf tests against your p95 token sizes (please share).

Option B — Adapter library (Concourse/ISV):
- What it does: measured client-side adapter that rewrites v3 calls to v4 before hitting Redwood.
- Pros: lower runtime cost on our side, clearer ownership for deprecation.
- Cons: requires partner upgrades and may fragment support.

Timeline recommendation:
- Prototype gateway shim: 3 weeks (prototype -> internal QA).
- Partner review + pilot: 2 weeks.
- Canary: 1 week at 1–5% traffic.
- Grace period before enforcement: recommend 120 days after public pilot to accommodate slow-moving ISVs.

Risks / items to validate:
- KV cache behavior for long-running streams (we may need to extend cache TTL for translated sessions).
- Billing alignment: confirm whether token accounting uses pre-translation or post-translation tokenization (we recommend post-translation billing, but that impacts partner pricing).

I attached a quick design draft and a small perf estimate sample (redwood_shim_design_draft.md, perf_estimates.csv). Happy to walk through today.

— Camila (Partner Eng)
attachments: redwood_shim_design_draft.md; perf_estimates.csv

Thanks Camila — that all sounds sensible. A few follow-ups from the Concourse product side:

1) Cost / billing: If Redwood bills on post-translation tokens, partners will expect clear guidance so they can reprice. Can you provide an example of the token delta for a 10k token p95 request?
2) SLA: If shim adds latency, will Redwood honor existing SLA commitments for partner-managed endpoints? If not, what will the SLA delta look like (we need to tell procurement).
3) Timeline: our initial ask from ISVs is to keep v3 behavior available until November 15th. Is that feasible?

I've attached a small impact workbook that our finance & procurement teams filled in (concourse_integration_impact.xlsx). Can we get conservative numbers to share?

— Erik
attachments: concourse_integration_impact.xlsx

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration: SDK v4 change — compatibility shim & SLA questions

Erik — thanks for the workbook and the questions. Confirming Redwood's provisional plan and the items we'll deliver so your procurement and ISVs can make decisions:

What we'll do (provisional, pending quick perf tests):
- Build a gateway shim prototype that does header translation + streaming frame translation. Prototype ETA: 2027-06-07.
- Run perf tests against a representative 10k-token payload and share p50/p95 deltas (target: p50 +<12ms, p95 +<40ms).
- Pilot/canary with Concourse: target pilot week 2027-06-14 (1–5% traffic).
- Public grace window (recommended): until 2027-10-15 enforcement. That gives ~150 days post-release for slow ISVs. If Concourse requires enforcement on 2027-11-15 we can discuss an extended window, but we should finalize by June so we can schedule capacity.
- Billing: we'll bill on post-translation tokens by default and include a token-delta example in the perf report. If partners require pre-translation billing we can discuss a commercial amendment (impacting deal RDW-3241).

Next steps for Concourse: share traffic profile (p50/p95 tokens), sample v3 request payloads, and confirm whether Concourse is comfortable with post-translation billing for the pilot.

I'll spin up the internal project ticket and assign Camila to the prototype. Laura, can you own comms and the partner-facing rollout note? David, can you confirm whether this needs an SLA exception approval from Product Ops?

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the initial tech sync (30m) and include a lightweight mutual action plan doc.

Best —
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
